---
title: "Seeded sampling verification and performance"
---

This benchmark times [seeded sampling](../rng.qmd) for the normal, beta, and Poisson families. [Raw results](rng-results.json) keep the seed, input hashes, numerical evidence, PHP version, binary hash, all timing samples, process elapsed time, and peak RSS.

## Methods

| Item | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Workloads | `dist_normal_rng`, `dist_beta_rng`, and `dist_poisson_rng` at 1,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000 draws, seed 42 |
| Machine | AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX virtual machine, 2 cores, 7.8 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64) |
| Software | PHP 8.5.12, phit 0.4.3 release build |
| Repetitions | One untimed warm-up, then five measurements |
| Statistic | Median milliseconds per full call |
| Timed | ChaCha setup from the seed, quantile evaluation, PHP result allocation, and reclamation of earlier results |
| Excluded | JSON input and output, and numerical summaries |
| Memory | Peak RSS of the whole worker process, from `peakmem` ([bench/peakmem.c](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/blob/main/bench/peakmem.c)) |

## Independent verification first

Before any timing phase, Python independently computes the ChaCha blocks at 17
evenly spaced indices, with the pinned PCG seed expansion/Open01 mapping. Base-R
quantiles transform those exact probabilities. PHP's sampled points must match
at `1e-15 + 1e-12*abs(reference)`; discrete values match the integer quantiles.
The full output is consumed by mean/variance calculations and checked against
theoretical moments within eight standard errors (using the distribution's fourth
central moment for variance). Fixed seeds make these checks deterministic.

This complements the ordinary 25-case independent stream/quantile fixture suite.
It does not compare every element to R and does not claim that R's own RNG shares
the ChaCha sequence. Each timed result undergoes the same numerical checks again.

## Timing interpretation

Peak RSS covers the whole worker, including summaries and inputs, not only the generator state. These are API-level times on the recorded machine, not throughput guarantees or a comparison with optimized rejection samplers. Every family uses inverse-CDF sampling, so the cost differences between families come from their quantile functions.

## Reproduction

Configure matching PHP/headers as in [development](../development.qmd). Python's
standard library and R/jsonlite are reference tools only.

```sh
cargo build -p phit --release --locked
PHP=/path/to/matching/php python3 tests/benchmarks/run-rng.py
python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py
```

The independent ChaCha equations are shared with the fixture generator and read no native uniforms or samples.
